subject: Re: Request throttling observed — decomposition, mitigation, and customer brief
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observed request throttling + P95 spike on gen-api

Quick summary: between 08:45-09:05 PDT we saw a correlated increase in request throttling and P95 latency for gen-api (streaming endpoints unaffected).

Key observations:
- QPS increased ~2.8x against normal baseline for the SignalWorks org (route: /v1/generate).
- Throttling at the router layer (504s/429s) correlates with backlog in the runtime scheduler; CPU and GPU utilization are normal.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped from 78% -> 42% at the same time window.
- P95 latency jumped from ~210ms -> ~1.6s for non-streaming calls.

Immediate ask: can product/engineers decide on temporary mitigations we can push in the next 30–45 minutes? Options I see:
  1) Enable a stricter per-tenant QPS gate for SignalWorks (drop/buffer) — buys isolation quickly.
  2) Route SignalWorks to the fallback model variant (smaller quantized) for 1 hour.
  3) Turn on prefix-based KV cache warmstart for their top prefixes (manual), which may restore hit-rate but needs runtime support.

I attached a quick qps summary and a stacktrace dump from the runtime worker that was symptomatic; more dumps available on request.

Soojin
SRE — Redwood Inference

Attachments: qps-summary-20280618.png, runtime-stacktrace.txt

Thanks — this looks like an isolation and cache-evaporation event that amplified with a sudden QPS burst. My priorities here: keep SignalWorks live (minimize errors), limit blast radius, and communicate clearly. Proposed play:

Action plan (short window: 0–1 hour)
- SRE: enable per-tenant QPS gate at router for SignalWorks to cap at their committed burst (soojin) — immediate.
- Runtime: prepare an automated route to fallback model variant (ben) — latch in 15–20m if gating doesn't stabilize.
- Product: approve soft-degradation note (explicitly describe the fallback, expected quality delta) and sign-off customer message (marissa/karthik). I drafted a short customer brief (attached) — please suggest edits.

Customer message goals:
- Acknowledge impact and show concrete mitigations (what we did, what we will do).
- Set expectations on quality when routed to fallback.
- Commit to timeline for returning to normal and a post-mortem.

Marissa — can you own the external comm? Karthik/Ben — confirm feasibility and rollback plan.

Priyom
Senior PM, Core Platform

Attachments: customer-note-draft.md

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed request throttling + P95 spike on gen-api

Priyom / Soojin — quick notes from the runtime side:
- Fallback routing to quantized-v2 is feasible; config exists and can be flipped at the router level with a single flag. Expected quality delta: minor for short prompts, more noticeable for long-context completions (we'll call this out).
- Prefix warmstart is non-trivial right now; it requires a targeted KV seeding job per tenant — I can run a manual seeding for SignalWorks but it'll take ~25m to complete and might not fully recover hit-rate for tail prefixes.
- Router gating can be applied immediately. I recommend: gate + manual KV seeding in parallel; if p95 remains >1s after 20m, flip routing to fallback.

Rollback plan: flip routing back to primary model when KV hit-rate >65% and p95 <350ms for 5 consecutive minutes. Automatic rollback should be manual-reviewed (Ben/Karthik).

I'll stand by to flip config and run the seeding job once we have sign-off.

—Ben
Runtime Engineering

From: Liz Barker <liz@signalworks.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service degradation seen this morning

Thanks for the quick note. We saw a bunch of 504s on our production rollout and customers are noticing. Impact: stalled onboarding flows, a handful of payment failures (external gateway), and higher support volume.

Please tell us: what is the experience if you route us to a fallback model? Will tokenization/format change? Will we need to change prompt templates? We need a clear statement for our engineering and CS teams so we can triage on our side if needed.

Liz Barker
Product Ops — SignalWorks

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Barker <liz@signalworks.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Consolidated update & customer brief — SignalWorks incident (June 18)

Liz — thanks for the note and sorry for the disruption. Below is the live update we are publishing to SignalWorks engineering and CS now. Marissa will post this to your PagerDuty/Intercom thread and copy your distribution list.

PUBLIC SUMMARY (short)
We observed an unexpected spike in request volume from your account that caused request gating at the router layer and degraded P95 latency for non-streaming generation calls between 08:45–09:10 PDT. Streaming endpoints were not affected. We have applied a temporary per-tenant QPS gate to stabilize traffic and prevent errors for other customers.

WHAT WE DID (actions taken)
- 09:05 PDT — applied per-tenant QPS gate to cap burst above contracted levels (isolates other tenants).
- 09:18 PDT — kicked off a manual KV cache seeding job for your top 50 prefixes (in progress, ~25m runtime).
- 09:35 PDT — prepared fallback routing to quantized-v2; held until we observed seeding impact.
- 09:58 PDT — after seeding improved hit-rate to ~66% and p95 returned <350ms, we removed fallback routing and eased the QPS gate.

EXPECTED EXPERIENCE IF ROUTED TO FALLBACK
- Model: the fallback uses quantized-v2 (smaller model weights).
- Prompts and tokenization: no changes required. Output quality: minor differences for short prompts, potentially more variance on very long-context prompts. We recommend testing representative prompts on a staging key if you want to evaluate quality impact.
- No prompt template changes are required; integration points remain the same.

NEXT STEPS
- Post-mortem (JIRA INF-4821) to be published in 72 hours with root cause analysis and long-term remediation proposals (routing heuristics, KV pre-warm policies).
- We will schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow to review mitigations and follow-ups. Priyom/Karthik/Ben will present technical findings; Marissa will own customer communication cadence.

If you want us to keep fallback routing enabled for an additional window for safety, say so and we will arrange it per your preference.

Apologies again — we are tracking this as a high-priority continuous improvement item and will send the post-mortem with metrics and remediation by Fri.
